title: Clarify when to use `getClaims` and `getUser` and discourage usage of `getSession`
body:
### Documentation is

- [x] Missing
- [x] Outdated
- [ ] Confusing
- [ ] Not sure?

### Explain in Detail

All of the Server Framework Documentation still uses `getUser()` by default, which means there is an extraneous call to the database. Supabase created `getClaims()` for this purpose increasing the speed and security of Supabase Auth. 

The docs should reflect this by default.

### Outdated Setup
- [NextJS](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/tutorials/with-nextjs?queryGroups=database-method&database-method=sql&queryGroups=language&language=ts) - see middleware.ts
- [SvelteKit](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/tutorials/with-sveltekit?queryGroups=database-method&database-method=sql) - see hooks.server.ts

### No Server Setup At All
- [Nuxt](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/tutorials/with-nuxt-3?queryGroups=database-method&database-method=sql) - this doesn't even have a server endpoint setup and is just a Vue setup
- [SolidJS](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/tutorials/with-solidjs?queryGroups=database-method&database-method=sql) - There should be a `SolidStart` version for server

The [@supabase/ssr]() makes it easy to add functionality to any framework, and could easily be used in place of outdated addons like:
- [Qwik Supabase](https://qwik.dev/docs/integrations/supabase/#supabase)
- [Nuxt Supabase](https://supabase.nuxtjs.org/)

I am happy to help create a demo for all of these if necessary (just let me know), but first *SvelteKit* and *NextJS* docs need to be updated with `getClaims()` instead of `getUser()`, and before `getClaims()` can be useful, the [typing problem](https://github.com/supabase/supabase-js/issues/1584) should be fixed.

J

comments.body:
@ChrisChinchilla - I saw you PR. You have:
```
Always use supabase.auth.getClaims() to protect pages and user data.
```
But, in fact, we DON'T want to do this. As it stands, it will ALWAYS run an extra fetch on each request, slowing down our apps. We ONLY want to run an extra fetch when the token is expired, or we are doing a secure action like change password.

I'm not sure if `getCliams()` iteself needs to be modified, or if `@supabase/ssr` needs to handle this differently? Either way, this definitely needs to be addressed.

Please advise.

J

It does do a fetch, but after the first one, the Supabase global cache should be kicking in, greatly reducing the latency - to single-digit ms, based on my experience.

I think the following has been said before, but neither `getClaims` or `getUser` are best for every situation.

Personally, with very little real-world experience mind you, I think `getClaims` should be the default in docs, but with a very visible disclaimer for when `getUser` is needed.

comments.author: jdgamble555
comments.body:
So `getClaims()` calls `getSession()` under the hood, which calls a number of other functions. `getSession()` calls the server regardless, which is different from the global `jwk()` cache.  It is still getting a new JWK from my understanding, but I would have to spend more time going through source code to confirm.

Assuming you're right, or this gets fixed, it still has two different problems.

1. We shouldn't have to think about which completely different function to run.  Maybe a `getUser(true)` for sensitive actions and just `getUser()` for regular actions (how Firebase handles it)
2. They return completely different types. This is not developer friendly and would require us to manually update our app to handle different return types.

J

comments.author: ChrisChinchilla
comments.body:
I have some further clarifications and questions from @jnschaeffer mostly aimed at your table @jdgamble555 

- Role / permissions: Is this referring to the role claim, which is actually about the Postgres role for the user? if so, that's not something the application should necessarily be concerned with (IMO) and is not so relevant with `getClaims`
- org_id / tenant info: these are user application-specific concerns. An application user has no relationship to a Supabase org. if the user wants these in a token, they would use app metadata or a [custom access token hook](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook) and get the data using `getClaims`.
- Email: should always be present in the token per [documentation](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/jwt-fields#required-claims), but may be stale. use getClaims when you want to get the value fast, and getUser if you need to ensure you are getting the freshest data
- Phone: same as for email
- Normal authorization logic: Not clear on what this means? The user could use `getClaims` to get token data to perform offline authorization (i.e., for real-time applications independent of the DB), but RLS would be used when interacting with the database and thus `getClaims` and `getUser` would be irrelevant

In summary, the best use case for `getClaims` is ensuring the user has a valid session before trying to interact with the project's data API so that the user doesn't get a bunch of 401 errors

Put more succinctly: `getClaims` is biased towards session validation, `getUser` is biased towards user record retrieval

Any thoughts? We have a project now scoped and all documentations that need updating recorded, so just getting any final input from the community.

Thanks!

comments.author: jdgamble555
comments.body:
@ChrisChinchilla 

- Role / Permissions: Not everyone uses RLS. RLS is a pain and not easy to implement, especially when you can just lock the table and use Drizzle or Supabase Admin directly on the server. In those cases, you would use the user id from the claim `user.sub` to create your own rules. There is also the `role` in the user table, which could be customized, but same scenario.
- org_id / tentant info: I removed that from the table, as more relevant to app_data.
- Email: Yes, always present, but again, for sensitive operations needing latest data, use getUser
- Phone: Not always present in either since phone is not required, hence, if embedded.
- Normal Authorization Logic: Here I am referring to normal database calls (not sensitive like password changes or pay-wall)

> The user could use getClaims to get token data to perform offline authorization (i.e., for real-time applications independent of the DB), but RLS would be used when interacting with the database and thus getClaims and getUser would be irrelevant

Not irrelevant at all.  Yes, if you're using supabase on the front end (like real time data), you MUST use RLS for proper security, however, an extra database call is very relevant. You don't want to call `getUser` which adds an extra fetch to the server when the claim is already in your session cookie.

> In summary, the best use case for getClaims is ensuring the user has a valid session before trying to interact with the project's data API so that the user doesn't get a bunch of 401 errors

Agreed, but we need something like my table (updated) to clarify the nuances.

> Put more succinctly: getClaims is biased towards session validation, getUser is biased towards user record retrieval

Almost, but one very large caveat. You need to validate the session with `getClaims()`, but you also need the user ID for querying the database (again, Drizzle is extremely popular with supabase, and supabase admin directly prevents having to think about complex RLS queries). Yes you want to use `getUser()` with user record retrieval, but also any secure data transactions when NOT using RLS.

You may me realize updating password or user table will use `getUser` anyway or latest session from database.

See [Updated Table](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/40985#issuecomment-3604234560) - probably need 2 tables, one with RLS, and one without.

I think as long as it is clear we are using RLS in the documentation, it is fine. However, any complex application is going to start using complex methods (RLS + Drizzle + Custom API points using Supabase Admin etc).

And a LOT of people like Drizzle.  Supabase still does not handle transactions on its own at all (you can't even do nested mutations like prisma), and very few people know how to write a custom function correctly, so Drizzle will be the way for any complex app.

A table similar to mine would definitely help.

J

comments.author: jdgamble555
comments.body: @its-kos - I think it depends on your app too in that scenario.  When you logout, you should get `null` for `getUser()` and `undefined` for `claims` in `getClaims()`.  If your app doesn't immediately refresh all server-side instances, then yes, you should use `getUser()` in those other scenarios, because a JWT could still be on the client. However, you should really be refreshing all your UI where this couldn't happen. What you're talking about would require you to use `getUser()` everywhere to be certain, so make sure you design your app correctly on top of all this so there can't be an invalid JWT just sitting around.

@Acccent - No, `getUser()` does not automatically refresh the JWT for `getClaims()` AFAICS in the [code](https://github.com/supabase/supabase-js/blob/c3189d620d7c34454b964d07c2d0d6e14f786a81/packages/core/auth-js/src/GoTrueClient.ts#L5793). You need to do this manually with `refreshSession()`.

@nandanosql @ChrisChinchilla - The problem is that you treat `getSession()` and `getUser()` as equally incorrect. `getUser()` needs to be in the docs as well, as there are several legitimate use cases. You DO NOT want to use `getClaims()` in all situations.

> It's safe to trust getClaims() because it validates the token in storage, either directly or by calling getUser() solely to check the result. It doesn't use the response from getUser() itself, only whether the validation succeeded.

This is in the Next Docs, which is blatantly incorrect. Maybe this is just unclear here?

It also looks like all you did is simplify the pages by replacing `getSession()` and `getUser()` with `getClaims()`, while also getting rid of middleware / hooks. You NEED middleware / hooks for `getUser()` --- to prevent extraneous calls to server with `getUser()`.

There are legitimate use cases for `getUser()`, which I mentioned in [this table](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/40985#issuecomment-3604234560). The table was not published [in favor of the docs being updated correctly](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/39947#issuecomment-3632928387).

Again, I provided a [perfect template](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/40985#issuecomment-3679073327) in SvelteKit, I am happy to do it for NextJS as well, but you guys have to accept ideas from other people, or come up with better ones...

After re-auditing the SDK source and the docs, here's the honest split:

Where you're right:
 - `creating-a-client.mdx:612` Nuxt server-route example still calls `supabase.auth.getUser()`, directly contradicting `:253` ("Always use `getClaims()`") in the same file.
 - `with-sveltekit.mdx:81` still tells the reader the TS compiler will complain about `event.locals.safeGetSession`, but the example `app.d.ts` no longer declares one. Stale prose.
 - Nuxt getting-started tutorial still has no server setup.
 - SolidJS tutorial still has no SolidStart variant.

We'll open a follow-up PR for these.

Where you're not right:
 - "`getClaims()` always calls `getSession()` which calls the server": it doesn't. `getSession()` reads from local storage; it only hits the network when `expires_at` is within the refresh margin (`GoTrueClient.ts:2963-2974`). On a valid token, zero network calls.
 - "`getClaims()` makes an extra fetch on every request": only on JWKS cache miss (one `/.well-known/jwks.json` fetch, then cached for `JWKS_TTL` — `GoTrueClient.ts:6180-6198`), or when using a symmetric signing secret / missing WebCrypto, where it falls back to `getUser()` (`:6322-6345`). On the modern asymmetric-keys path with a warm cache it is fully local. j4w8n had this right upthread.
 - The typing concern (supabase-js#1584) shipped in supabase-js#1802 on 2025-11-06.

Where it's opinion, not bug:
 - Collapsing `getUser`/`getClaims`/`getSession` into one `getUser(forceRefresh)` is an API-design preference, not a defect.
   The three methods answer three different questions (server-validated user record / locally-verified JWT claims / raw session). We're not planning to collapse them.

Thank you for bearing with us, and thank you very much for your constructive feedback. I am reopening to address the first 4 points.
